summary: Frontend-only verification of Markdown Write/Preview + page-purpose captions on Kodama Talk. 26/26 targeted checks pass. All Markdown constructs (h1/h2/h3, strong, em, code, safe links with target=_blank + rel=noopener noreferrer nofollow, blockquote, ul, ol) render as real HTML in door-preview and in message bubbles. Preview guard on empty composer works. Landing, Shelf and Stream purpose captions render correctly. Regression flows (address entry, owner unlock, drop send) intact.

issues: stream-purpose falls back to conversation.subtitle when present. For the seeded /alex → Mara Direct Talk, the subtitle is 'talk.kodama.page/mara' (the counterpart address) rather than a plain-language purpose like 'A private conversation that began with a Drop'. Purely a copy consideration — the spec permits subtitle fallback, so this is informational only.

critical_code_review_comments: markdown.tsx uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Current sanitizer escapes HTML first and only permits http(s) hrefs, which is safe. Consider adding a unit test for adversarial inputs (e.g. javascript:, data:, mixed **/*/backtick edge cases) as a regression guard.

The italic rules use a leading class '(^|[\s(])' which means '_italic_' at the very start of a paragraph is handled, but consecutive markers in an inline sequence like '_a_ _b_' may only match the first because the leading whitespace requirement collides with the previously consumed char. Consider expanding to allow inline chains, or add a test.

streamPurpose() default is used only when conversation.subtitle is null/undefined. Seeded direct-talks include address strings as subtitles which override the friendlier purpose. Consider suppressing subtitle-as-purpose for 'direct' kind, or introducing a separate 'subtitle' vs 'purpose' field.
test_credentials: Owner unlock for /alex: any 4+ char password (used 'secret').
